rucam.l: ALT. Scores nothing directly; it is half the R ratio that selects the scoring table.
The laboratory upper limit of normal for ALT.
ALP. Scores nothing directly; it is the other half of the R ratio.
The laboratory upper limit of normal for ALP.
Time to onset. THE DAY WINDOWS AND POINTS DEPEND ON THE SCALE the R ratio selected. Two values EXCLUDE the case rather than scoring it.
Course after stopping the drug. THE VALID VALUES DIFFER BY SCALE: the hepatocellular table runs -2 to +3 over 30 days, the cholestatic 0 to +2 over 180 days.
Alcohol use, or pregnancy on the cholestatic scale. ONE SHARED LINE worth 1 point, and the risk domain is capped at 2.

Concomitant drugs [none-or-incompatible = No concomitant drug, or timing incompatible (0); compatible-timing = Concomitant drug with compatible or suggestive timing (-1); known-hepatotoxin = Known hepatotoxin with compatible timing (-2); proven-cause = Concomitant drug with evidence for its role (positive rechallenge or validated test) (-3)]. Reaches -3.

Exclusion of other causes [all-excluded = All group I and group II causes excluded (2); group1-excluded = All 6 group I causes excluded (1); four-or-five-excluded = Only 4 or 5 group I causes excluded (0); fewer-than-four = Fewer than 4 group I causes excluded (-2); alternative-highly-probable = An alternative cause is highly probable (-3)]. Reaches -3.
Previous information on hepatotoxicity [labeled = Reaction is in the product label (2); published = Published case reports, but not labeled (1); unknown = No published association (0)]

Response to readministration [positive = Doubling of the relevant test with the drug alone (3); compatible = Doubling with the drug given again alongside the one already in use (1); negative = Given again after recovery with no rise (-2); not-done = Not done, or not interpretable (0)]. SCORED BECAUSE IT SOMETIMES HAPPENS, NOT BECAUSE IT IS ADVISABLE.
